INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  Library Board
  MINUTES – November 20, 2019

The Inglewood Library Board met on November 20, 2019 in the Gladys Waddingham Lecture Hall. The
meeting was called to order at 6:32 p.m. by Board Member Pat Douglas.

Roll Call

Present:
  Patt Sanders – At Large Board Member, Chairman
  Julie Minton – District 1 Board Member, Vice Chairman
  Pat Douglas – District 2 Board Member
  Ernesto Castillo – District 3 Board Member

Absent Board Members:
  Jacqueline Cochran – District 4 Board Member

Staff:
  Harjinder Singh – Deputy to the City Manager
  Frances Tracht – Library Manager
  Irina Martirosian – Staff Assistant

Absent Staff:
  Sabrina Barnes – Parks, Recreation and Community Services Director

Approval of the Minutes

  Board Member Douglas made a motion for the approval of the minutes for October 23, 2019;
Board Member Castillo seconded the motion. Minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Library Board Members Minton, Castillo and Douglas
  Nays: None

Library Report

  Deputy to the City Manager Harjinder Singh gave an update on the renovation of the Main Library.
The City is moving forward with the process of hiring an architectural firm. The architectural and
management agreements are due in mid-December. Some of those teams are very good and City is
looking forward to working with them.
  Board member Douglas got a flyer in the mail that spoke about the money the City received from
the State, which is mainly for affordable housing and asked if part of that $100 million dollars is allocated

  1
 towards the affordable housing as well or the library renovation only. Singh explained that the library project
was approved prior to the availability of these funds.
  Library Manager Francis Tracht talked about Holiday Hours. Library staff is excited about the
changes; are meeting more frequently to discuss what needs to be done to prepare for the move; trying to
buy less books; concentrating more on programming for next year; and are very close to the end of the
weeding project.

Friends Report

  Susan Carleo, President of the Friends of Inglewood Public Library (FOIPL) introduced the five
other FOIPL Board members present and reviewed FOIPL’s purpose with the Board. FOIPL serves as the
non-profit dedicated to raising funds for the Inglewood Public Library. They operate with an all-volunteer
Board and raise funds by selling books that have been donated by the community to help the library.
  FOIPL requires the following to continue their work during the construction period and in the newly
revitalized library:
   a place to receive donated books
   a work area to sort and store books
   a public sales area to display books with a secure way to collect funds from daily sales; and
   a designated area to hold quarterly book sales.

  Friends of Inglewood Public Library currently focuses on only book sales because it is the most
cost-effective way to achieve their fundraising goals.
  Carleo said they are honored to be part of the discussion to revitalize the library and confident that
they can continue to raise funds for the library as long as the four conditions described above can
reasonably be met; and they are looking forward to continuing their work which represents a way to help
the library through donated books and by providing a way for our community to buy books at a very low-
cost.
  Carleo also announced that the FRIENDS' Annual Winter Holiday Book Sale will be held on
Saturday, Dec. 14 from 10-3 in the library depository. All are asked to share the attached flyer to help
spread the word.

Public Comments

  Gregory Mason voiced his concern about gentrification in the city.

Commissioner Comments

  Board member Sanders talked about herself being a little skeptical about moving forward without
having a library director, thanked Harjinder and said that she was happy about the strategic plan that it’s
moving forward.
  Board member Castillo thanked Susan Carleo for her dedicated work, for bringing board members
to the meeting and is happy to work with good people who are honestly looking for the betterment of the
library.
  Board member Minton thanked Friends of Inglewood Public Library for their dedicated work and is
happy that once the new library is built, Friends will be a larger group and a lot more people will be
involved.
  2
 Board member Douglas also thanked Susan Carleo and Harjinder Singh for doing a great job.
Next meeting will be in January. Everyone wished Happy Holidays to each other.

With no further comments the meeting was adjourned at 6:56 p.m.
